Name: Durumi Hut - Harvest Helpers and Bucket Watering
Author: asb3967
Description:
[b]Durumi Hut 1.6.0 - Familiar little helpers, smoother routines and festival clothes[/b]
Build a home for the same red-bereted helpers who harvest your crops and carry water from their well. This update refines their existing movements and decisions, adds eight festival clothing designs, and gives desk writing its own pencil-and-paper animation. The room, child proportions and native pixel density remain consistent.

Also included since the public 1.4 release: useful farming work practice, winter snowball play, summer soap bubbles, and expanded winter activity frames. Previously taught huts keep their lessons.

[b]Festival clothing follows the original calendar[/b]
Eight clothing designs fit the existing motions: Egg Festival (Spring 13), Flower Dance (Spring 24), Luau (Summer 11), Moonlight Jellies (Summer 28), Stardew Valley Fair (Fall 16), Spirit's Eve (Fall 27), Festival of Ice (Winter 8) and Winter Star (Winter 25).

New directional clothing guides supply spring shirts and vests, summer beach clothes, autumn outfits and warm winter coats. Garment fabric is registered to the existing motion frames, preserving the child's body, hair, red beret, hands and props. These are not eight wholly redrawn animation sets. Passive festivals reuse related outfits: Desert Festival uses the fair set, Trout Derby the luau set, SquidFest the ice set, and Night Market the Winter Star set. Native game dates and unlock conditions apply; an inaccessible desert does not activate its outfit. Outdoor raincoats take priority, winter coats remain warm, and the normal sleeping pose is preserved. The children stay near their home; this does not send them fishing or travelling to festival grounds.

[b]Better movement and task decisions[/b]
Bucket carrying, play, and trips through the hut door retry a clear route when a new obstacle or the player blocks progress. Collisions stay active, with a timeout for genuinely unreachable routes. If the farmer or a sprinkler waters a target while a child is carrying water to it, the child keeps the remaining water and chooses a dry crop instead of wasting a pour.

Only the workers needed for available watering targets leave the hut. A worker who does not receive a job actually returns through the door, preserving the same indoor/outdoor population. A play session also ends if the day changes to a traditional festival. Walking speed, range, crew limits and the eight-target bucket do not increase.

Everyday idle includes a small blink and a quiet gesture with staggered timing between children. Writing has dedicated pencil-and-paper frames in both everyday and winter clothing. Reading and page turns keep their book poses; the existing furniture and shared bed remain in place.

[b]Farming lessons help with real hand work[/b]
Your farmer teaches up to two Farming levels below their base level, capped at 8. The learned level affects native crop quality and level-dependent yield. Existing 1.4 and 1.5 learned levels are retained.

The included work-practice feature adds a clearly defined mod lesson for work practice: the teacher's reference is 4 percentage points per base Farming level, then 20 percentage points are withheld, up to a 20% action-time reduction. A level 10 farmer's 40% reference becomes 20% for the child. This is a task-specific adaptation, not a claim that vanilla Farming or Artisan gives this action-speed bonus. The helpers do not chop wood, mine, fight, fish or process artisan goods.

At taught level 8, normal crop-picking actions take about 1.6 seconds instead of 2; well filling takes 720ms instead of 900 and pouring 640ms instead of 800. The full preparation/commit/finish sequence remains. Walking, range, crew size, bucket capacity 8, fertilizer, storage and the player's own stats are unchanged. The existing Skills face shows the learned level, action reduction and fill/pour durations.

[b]Spare-time seasonal play[/b]
When no eligible crop or watering task is waiting, available children can walk through the hut door to a clear, reachable 5x3 play patch near the hut. Winter snowball play requires actual local snowfall and at least two available children. Summer bubbles work in dry, non-lightning weather. Some children may keep reading indoors. There are no extra workers, new output items, crop damage, combat hits or rewards.

Short play bouts can start 10:00-11:30 or 14:00-17:30, followed by a break. New eligible work interrupts play; weather changes, unsafe space, dinner and bedtime bring the crew home. If there is no safe play area, they stay indoors. Heavy chores are not part of the children's role.

[b]Seasonal motion improvements included from 1.5[/b]
The seasonal-play update added 96 new registered native-pixel poses across snow play, bubbles and winter indoor life. Winter reading, eating, drinking and washing now have paired poses. Winter beret adjustments and yawns have their own gestures instead of the washing pose. Unladen seasonal walking uses its existing passing pose without confusing the bucket-pouring frame. All new cells retain integer pixels, complete silhouettes, consistent pivots and the original palette. Reading and page turns use book poses; desk writing now has its own pencil frames. These remain visual routines, not a crafting simulation.

[b]Retained hut features[/b]
[b]Life inside the hut[/b]
Walk through the hut door to meet the same helpers who work in your fields. At midday they can share a meal, and at 9 pm or later each helper settles at their own pillow beneath the patchwork quilt. The base hut uses two places in the shared bed; an expanded hut uses three.

The room follows the creator's illustrated layout: a continuous kitchen counter, central dining table, shared canopy bed, bookcases, tea table by the hearth and a study. Chairs and bedding have separate foreground pieces so helpers sit behind the slats and sleep beneath the quilt. Paths lead to their actual furniture and seats. Meals and washing are visual routines; they do not consume crops or produce cooking items.

The indoor harvest box opens the hut's shared 36-slot storage. The study control pauses or resumes harvesting. Inspect the globe, bookcase or kitchen stove for different lines. Reading and page-turning share book poses. Writing uses separate pencil-and-paper frames in everyday and winter clothing; winter indoor activities also use directional poses for books, meals, drinks and washing.

[b]Rain and winter[/b]
Rainy mornings start indoors. If rain begins while the helpers are outside, they wear yellow raincoats and physically return through their door. Winter helpers rest inside, with short snowfall play and warm-clothed watering trips when conditions allow; they return afterward. Indoor and outdoor helpers are one native population, with no extra work crew.

Harvesters rest in rain, winter and on traditional festival days. The well upgrade's watering runs independently from 6 am until 7 pm on dry days, including winter and festivals when eligible crops need water. Rain stops watering.

[b]Build and upgrade[/b]
Robin offers the hut without wizard-quest, year or season unlocks. Normal shop hours and construction scheduling apply. The original Junimo Hut remains available.

[list]
[*]Base: a 13×13 area centered on the door, up to 2 helpers. Costs 20,000g, 200 stone, 9 starfruit and 100 fiber; takes 2 days.[/*]
[*]First upgrade: a 17×17 area and up to 3 helpers. Costs 5,000g, 100 wood and 100 stone; takes 1 day.[/*]
[*]Second upgrade: the same area and crew, plus a small well and bucket watering. Costs 10,000g, 200 stone, 5 iron bars and 10 hardwood; takes 2 days.[/*]
[/list]Each exterior building occupies 3×2 tiles. The working area includes the building.

[b]Physical bucket watering[/b]
Helpers fill buckets at the well, carry water to a crop and pour before its soil becomes wet. One bucket waters up to 8 targets before refilling. Filling, walking and pouring take time, and the same maximum of 3 helpers also handles harvesting.

Growing crops, trellis crops, wild seeds and outdoor garden pots are eligible. Dead crops, empty soil, already-wet soil and crops that need no water are skipped. A reachable route is required. The harvest toggle is independent of watering.

[b]Install and update[/b]
Use your own Stardew Valley 1.6.15 installation and SMAPI 4.5.2. Content Patcher is not required. Close the game, move the old DurumiHut folder outside Mods, then extract the new DurumiHut folder into Mods. Existing standalone installations can replace DurumiHut-Standalone/Mods/DurumiHut. Launch through SMAPI. Existing huts remain in the save; teach them from the Farming row if they have not learned yet. Previously saved 1.4 and 1.5 lessons persist.

This is the standard mod ZIP with source and build instructions. No proprietary Stardew game files are distributed. Install SMAPI from [url=https://smapi.io/]its official site[/url].

[b]Previous installer warning:[/b] Nexus quarantined the earlier optional Windows installer. Its executable has detections from multiple security engines, and those detections have not been established as false positives. The replacement installer remains withheld. Use the standard ZIP; do not disable protection or bypass quarantine to run the old executable.

Personal items obstructed by the updated room's walls, fixtures or exit are recovered with their contents at the Lost and Found in the Mayor's Manor. A farmer loaded at an obsolete blocked position moves to the entrance. To remove the mod, empty storage, leave the room, demolish all Durumi Huts through Robin while the mod is enabled, and save a day. Close the game, then remove the mod folder.

[b]Twelve languages[/b]
Construction menus, furniture, room interactions and teaching follow the language selected in Stardew Valley: English, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Turkish and Simplified Chinese. A quick-start guide in all twelve languages is included. Translations are AI-assisted; full native-speaker proofreading is not claimed.

[b]AI disclosure and credits[/b]
This is an [b]unofficial Drami fan creation[/b]. Durumi is a user-defined ten-year-old child with an androgynous appearance, a red beret and short white hair. The player farmer and ordinary Junimos retain their original appearances.

The commissioning user supplied the character setting, Life Pack and illustrated room layout. OpenAI Codex and GPT-6 Astra assisted code, review, translations, documentation and testing. OpenAI's built-in image generation created or edited original helper and hut artwork. AI-Generated Content and AI Media apply. Gameplay screenshots are actual game captures; labeled concept artwork is illustrative. No endorsement by the game developer or streamer is claimed.

Stardew Valley belongs to ConcernedApe. SMAPI is maintained by Pathoschild and contributors. The mod loads the game's assets from the player's installation. The archive includes the mod's source and build instructions.

[b]Validation and limits[/b]
The supported inspection environment is Windows single-player, Stardew Valley 1.6.15 and SMAPI 4.5.2. Multiplayer, compatibility with other Junimo overhauls and every mod combination are unverified. Please report reproducible issues with relevant SMAPI logs, keeping private save and account data out of public posts.
